newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees no change in next Shuttle-Mir mission.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees no change in next Shuttle-Mir mission.

text.p: The next U.S. Shuttle mission to Russia's Mir space station will go ahead as planned in September despite a series of accidents at the orbital complex that still need repairs, Russian officials said on Monday.

"On September 17, the next Shuttle should be launched so as to dock with the Mir space station on September 20," Mir mission director Vladimir Solovyov told a news conference at Mission Control outside Moscow. NASA astronaut Wendy Lawrence is in training at Russia's Star City to go aboard Mir in September.
Lawrence, a 37-year-old commander in the U.S. navy, is scheduled to spend four months on Mir.
She is due to replace Michael Foale, 40, a British-born astrophycist who has been on Mir since flying up on a previous shuttle flight in May.
Foale's current Russian crewmates on Mir, Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin, were told on Monday they would fly home on August 14, nearly two weeks ahead of schedule.
First they will hand over to Anatoly Solovyov and Pavel Vinogradov, who blast off aboard a Russia Soyuz craft on August 5.
